lines.trans: Boss, sorry to keep you waiting. It's the hugely popular yogurt flavor.
Did you buy only the yogurt flavor?
Yes, because this one is the most delicious.
What are you going to do if someone dislikes yogurt flavor?
If you want to make it in this world, use your imagination to make people happy.
Please get today's appearance fees ready.
Understood. Please set it down there, I'll drink it later.
I joined the company as Mr. Muranishi's assistant. Nice to meet you.
Everyone's appearance fees come to 140 million yen.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Past 覚えた means 'I have memorized it' (and therefore now know it).

examples.text: 新しい言葉を覚えます。

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Humble noun form of 待たせる, used in apologies like お待たせしました.

examples.text: 大変お待たせいたしました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for waiting.

examples.text: お待たせしてすみません。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: 黒木さんは一躍人気ですけど、撮影現場はどういう感じなんですか？
examples.trans: You shot to stardom overnight—what does it feel like on a film set?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 社長、お待たせしました。ちまたで大人気のヨーグルト味です。
examples.trans: Boss, sorry to keep you waiting. It's the hugely popular yogurt flavor.

examples.text: お前、ヨーグルト味だけを買ってきたのか？
examples.trans: Did you buy only the yogurt flavor?

examples.text: ヨーグルト味を嫌いな人がいたらどうするんだよ？
examples.trans: What are you going to do if someone dislikes yogurt flavor?

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.trans: If you want to make it in this world, use your imagination to make people happy.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).
